standard.title: First Nations dance and Country/Place
standard.description: explore how First Nations Australians use dance to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored examples of dance choreographed and/or performed by First Nations Australians (Y1-2). They can observe element use in First Nations dance and know that First Nations Australians use dance on significant cultural occasions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how First Nations Australians use dance to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place.

nodes.label: Connection and responsibility through dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how First Nations Australians use dance to express connection to and responsibility for Country/Place, culture and people.
nodes.minimum_width: Describing at least one way in which a First Nations Australian dance communicates connection to or responsibility for Country/Place — using a specific example.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring how First Nations Australians use dance to express connection to and responsibility for Country/Place: communicating knowledge about local seasons, wind, water, fire, sustainable practices; exploring dances with representatives of First Nations Australian communities or via resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians.
wider: Collect and share information about dances performed by First Nations Australians at festivals or ceremonies — reflecting on how these dances communicate knowledge about Country/Place
Explore screen-based storytelling used by First Nations Australians to maintain unique ways of life — comparing with dance forms used for similar purposes
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a genuine conceptual grasp of connection and responsibility as expressed through dance, students cannot move beyond surface observation. This understanding is the foundation for the more analytical engagement required in Y5-6 (revitalising cultures) and Y7-8 (ICIP rights).

response_modes.reason: Connection and responsibility are concepts that require explicit unpacking — they are not self-evident from observation alone. Use guided discussion and resources created by First Nations Australians to build conceptual understanding before asking students to describe it.
Exploring multiple examples of how different First Nations communities use dance to express their relationship to Country/Place prevents conflation of all First Nations Australian cultures.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who encounter multiple examples of First Nations Australian dance connecting to Country/Place develop genuine understanding of the diversity of First Nations cultures and the specificity of those connections — essential for respectful engagement throughout F-10.
success_criteria: Student can explain what 'connection to Country/Place' means in the context of First Nations Australian dance
Student can describe how at least one specific dance communicates this connection

nodes.label: Elements communicating Country/Place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how specific element choices in First Nations Australian dance communicate knowledge about Country/Place.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least one element of dance used in a First Nations Australian dance and explaining how it communicates something about Country/Place.
nodes.typical_width: Observing how elements of dance (movement, space, time, dynamics) are used in dances choreographed and performed by First Nations Australians to communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place — e.g. how movements represent wind, water, fire, or seasonal knowledge; exploring movements with community representatives or through co-created resources.
wider: Compare element use across two First Nations Australian dances from different communities — identifying how different environmental or seasonal knowledge is communicated through different element choices
Explore cultural accounts of Country/Place through dance with community representation — noticing how specific movement types carry specific knowledge

response_modes.reason: Reading element use as culturally meaningful — not just aesthetically interesting — requires a specific observational frame. Scaffold with focused questions: 'What in the movement shows us something about this place?', 'What do you think this movement represents?'

success_criteria: Student can identify at least one element choice in a First Nations Australian dance and explain what it communicates about Country/Place
Student engages with First Nations dance content with respect — uses appropriate terminology and follows any protocols introduced
